wstep: There is no recipe here for sprats and herring smoked at home, including whole, ungutted fish. [T:-]

ostrzezenia.tekst: According to the FDA, gut any fish before salting, drying, pickling or fermenting it. [T:MIE-061]
The FDA considers uneviscerated (ungutted) fish that are salt-cured, dried or smoked a potentially life-threatening health hazard. [T:MIE-067]

akapity: According to FDA guidance for seafood processors, small uneviscerated fish under 5 inches, such as anchovies and sprats, may be left ungutted only under process controls that need measured salt, water activity or pH; JarAtlas has no home method to check them. [T:MIE-066]
According to the FDA, such ungutted fish products are hazardous whether they are stored at room temperature, in the refrigerator or in the freezer. [T:MIE-070]
The FDA will consider seizing uneviscerated salt-cured, dried or smoked fish more than 5 inches long that are sold between states; this is a legal threshold, not a safety limit. [T:MIE-069]
JarAtlas has found no tested home recipe for smoking ungutted sprats or herring from a checked source. [T:-]
Wisconsin Sea Grant and University of Minnesota Extension have a method for hot smoking fish at home that has been scientifically tested for safety. [T:MIE-072]
In that method, the fish are first gutted and gilled, the kidney is removed from the belly cavity, and all exposed surfaces are rinsed with fresh water. [T:MIE-143]
For gutted fish, follow the full tested hot-smoking method on JarAtlas’s separate cards, not only its temperature step. [T:-]
JarAtlas describes hot smoking of some gutted fish, such as mackerel, on separate cards. [T:-]
